title: Feuquières to Catinat, Pignerol, 25 January 1691, in the petit chiffre of the Pignerol governors

documents.shelfmark: Mémoires et correspondance du maréchal de Catinat (1819) t. II pp. 283-284 (original: SHD, dépôt de la guerre)

plaintext.source: Bazeries deciphered it c. 1893 (Le Masque de fer p. 272) but never published the text

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's transcription collated with MDZ page images of the 1819 print

documents.shelfmark: Mémoires et correspondance du maréchal de Catinat (1819) t. I pp. 140-141

plaintext.source: Contemporary 'traduction' printed with it in the 1819 Mémoires t. I pp. 141-142; a free rendering, not verbatim

system.summary: Two-part code of 367 groups: letters with 2-5 homophones mostly below 100, CV syllables, words and nulls scattered above.
system.sibling_key: Bazeries' Grand Chiffre de 1691 (587 groups) gave the design; the d'Herleville letter in the same petit chiffre with its translation gave the values. Both used.
system.notes: i/j and u/v merged; numbers and place names spelled. Key recovered for 167 of 179 groups used.

prior_solution.where: Bazeries' unpublished decipherment (1893), presumably in his papers at SHD Vincennes; not found

conditions.human_role: Supplied the Gallica PDF of Burgaud and Bazeries, Le Masque de fer (1893).

solution.what: Collated Tomokiyo's transcription with the 1819 page images: three corrections.
418 groups, 160 distinct, max 366; 46 % below 100; no Croissy step-10 structure: two-part code with letters low.
Matched control of the inferred design: the solver's wrong keys outscore the true key; 4-12 % recovery; 60 % of key given completes only 63 %.
Annealing with Veillane cribs and word-segmentation objective on the real letter: crib-farmed word salad.
Read Bazeries' Le Masque de fer (1893): he deciphered the letter with a 367-group petit chiffre; neither text nor table printed.
Transcribed Bazeries' Grand Chiffre table and verified it on four 1690-91 despatches: gives the design.
MDZ OCR of the 1819 Mémoires searched for number runs: found Louvois to d'Herleville (6 Sept 1690) in the same code with its translation.
Exact known-plaintext alignment and annealers against the translation.
Hand anchoring of the d'Herleville second paragraph and propagation between the two letters.
Both letters read: 586 of 601 tokens, 167 of 179 groups.
d'Herleville reading matches its printed translation; Feuquières text matches Catinat's Veillane memoir of 19 Jan.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The petit chiffre was rebuilt by aligning Louvois's letter to d'Herleville of 6 Sept 1690, printed in the same code with its translation in the 1819 Mémoires de Catinat (t. I pp. 140-142), and carrying the values over to the Feuquières letter; Bazeries' Grand Chiffre table gave only the design.
outcome.notes: 586 of 601 tokens over the two letters (NOTES); 12 groups unread, singletons or nulls.
